setTableRemarks.remarks: Files LexaVault produced or kept for a document (original, extracted text, findings, redacted copy and others), one row per file.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the artifact.
The entity (tenant) the artifact belongs to.
The document this artifact was made from or belongs to.
Kind of file: ORIGINAL, EXTRACTED_TEXT, EXTRACTED_TEXT_BATCH, FINDINGS_BATCH, VISION_PAGE, OCR_TEXT, REDACTED, DERIVED_REDACTED and others.
State of the file: GENERATING, AVAILABLE, FAILED or DELETED.
Which file store holds the file, used with storage_key to find it and its stored_files record.
Bucket or container within the file store, empty when the store has none.
Path or key of the file within the store, matched to stored_files to know how it is protected.
Media type of the file, for example application/pdf.
Size of the file in bytes.
Algorithm used for checksum_value, for example SHA-256.
Checksum of the file content, used to check it has not changed.
When the artifact was created.
When the artifact row was last changed.
Optimistic locking counter, increased on every update.

setTableRemarks.remarks: The audit trail: one row per action a person or machine took, with its outcome, kept for compliance and reports.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the audit record.
The entity (tenant) the action took place in.
The person or machine that performed the action.
What was done, as an action code.
Kind of object the action was on, for example a case or document.
Id of the object the action was on.
Result of the action: SUCCESS, FAILURE, DENIED or PARTIAL.
Id shared by all records and events from the same request, used to trace one operation.
Extra detail about the action in text form, holding codes, counts and ids rather than document values (to confirm).
When the action happened.
When the audit record was written.
The person's display name at the time of the action, empty for records written before task 0016.
The case (package) id the Cases page shows, at the time of the action, never a business identifier.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Where each case's instructions file is stored, one row per case, the text itself is kept encrypted in the file and in no column.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: The case (document package) the instructions belong to.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
Id of the stored instructions file, replaced when the instructions are changed.
Which file store holds the instructions file.
Bucket or container within the file store, empty when the store has none.
Path or key of the instructions file within the store.
When the instructions were last saved.

setTableRemarks.remarks: A case's priority when it is not the default NORMAL, kept apart from document_packages so processing cannot undo a reviewer's change.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: The case (document package) this priority is for.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
The case's priority: URGENT, NORMAL, LOW or BULK.
When the priority was last set.
The source the case came from (an integration connection id, or folder:key for a watched folder), used for Bulk sources.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Catalog of versioned document intelligence bundles (model, prompt, rule and threshold versions), with the frozen baseline as safe fallback.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique version name of the bundle, referenced by entity policies and processing snapshots.
Lifecycle state of the bundle: CANDIDATE, PROMOTED or RETIRED.
Version of the AI model the bundle uses.
Version of the AI prompts the bundle uses.
Version of the sensitive data detectors the bundle uses.
Version of the OCR rules the bundle uses.
Version of the document profile content the bundle uses, none for the baseline.
Version of the validation rules the bundle uses.
Version of the confidence thresholds the bundle uses.
Short human description of the bundle.
When the bundle was added to the catalog.
When the bundle was promoted for use, empty while it is a candidate.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Cases: one row per document package taken in, grouping its documents through processing, review, export and deletion.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the case, shown as the case ID on the Cases page.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
How the case came in: MANUAL_UPLOAD, FOLDER_INTAKE, API_SUBMISSION or SCANNER_INTAKE.
Case state, such as CREATED, PROCESSING, PENDING_REVIEW, IN_REVIEW, APPROVED, REJECTED, FAILED or CANCELLED.
Extra key-value metadata of the case (classification, tags, context) as JSON.
The person or machine actor that created the case.
When the case was created.
When the case row was last changed.
Optimistic locking counter, increased on every update.
The business record this case is linked to through its business identifiers, empty when not linked.
Hash of the intake source and attempt, unique per entity, used so the same submission is not taken in twice.
Reference to where the case came from, such as a sender's package reference or folder path.
When a person hid the case from the dashboard, empty while it is shown.
The person who hid the case from the dashboard.
Level sent by the source and passed on at export, never changed by LexaVault: STANDARD, CONFIDENTIAL or HIGHLY_CONFIDENTIAL.

setTableRemarks.remarks: How each page of a document is read (fast text path or vision model) and why, deleted with its document, no page text.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: The entity (tenant) the document belongs to.
The document the page belongs to.
Page number within the document, starting at 1.
How the page is read: FAST, FAST_SIGNATURE or VISION.
Why the page took its path, names joined by +, such as PICTURE, HANDWRITING, LOW_OCR_CONFIDENCE or CHECK_FAILED.
Mean OCR word confidence for the page from 0 to 1, empty when the routing checks did not need OCR.
Boxes the signature detector found on the page, each as left,top,width,height, used to cover signatures.
When the page route was recorded.

setTableRemarks.remarks: The documents (PDF files) of each case, with their processing state.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the document.
The entity (tenant) the document belongs to.
The case (document package) the document belongs to.
Kind of file: PDF, IMAGE, WORD, SPREADSHEET, TEXT, EMAIL or OTHER.
Processing state: UPLOADED, EXTRACTING, DETECTING, REDACTING, PROCESSED or FAILED.
File name of the document as received.
Media type of the received file, for example application/pdf.
Size of the received file in bytes.
Algorithm used for checksum_value, for example SHA-256.
Checksum of the received file, used to check its integrity.
Number of pages in the document, 0 until it is known.
When the document was taken in.
When the document row was last changed.
Optimistic locking counter, increased on every update.
Level sent by the source and passed on at export, never changed by LexaVault: STANDARD, CONFIDENTIAL or HIGHLY_CONFIDENTIAL.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Sensitive information found in documents, one row per item with its place on the page and review state, never the value itself.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the finding.
The document the finding is in.
Kind of sensitive information, such as PERSON_NAME, SSN, DATE_OF_BIRTH, ADDRESS, SIGNATURE or UNREAD_PAGE.
Page number the finding is on, starting at 1.
Character position where the finding starts in the page text.
Character position where the finding ends in the page text.
How sure the detector is, from 0 to 1, used to decide between automatic redaction and review.
Name of the detector or rule that found it.
Version of the detector that found it.
Review state: DETECTED, CONFIRMED, DISMISSED, REDACTED or OVERRIDDEN.
When the finding was detected.
When the finding was last changed.
Optimistic locking counter, increased on every update.
The entity (tenant) the finding belongs to.
Left edge of the box to redact, as a share of page width from 0 to 1, empty when there is no box.
Top edge of the box to redact, as a share of page height from 0 to 1, empty when there is no box.
Width of the box to redact, as a share of page width, empty when there is no box.
Height of the box to redact, as a share of page height, empty when there is no box.
What read the value: PDF_TEXT, OCR, VISION, FORM_FIELD, SIGNATURE, PAGE_CHECK or PERSON, empty for findings before task 0105.
How it was found: PATTERN, AI_MODEL, CHECK or PERSON, empty for findings before task 0105.
How its place on the page was found, such as READER_WORDS, MODEL_BOX, MATCHED_WORDS, GENEROUS_COVER, NONE or PERSON.
Why a person is needed, naming the placement step that failed, empty when no person is needed.
The person who placed or drew the box, empty when LexaVault placed it.
When the person placed or drew the box.
Redaction style in force when the document was searched, such as KEEP_LAST_FOUR, empty means removed in full.
Which path(s) found it, names joined by +, such as TEXT, VISION or SIGNATURE, empty for older and person-drawn findings.
The AI model(s) that took part in finding it, names and versions only, empty when no model took part.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Domain events written in the same transaction as the change that caused them, for later publishing (outbox pattern).

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the event.
The entity (tenant) the event belongs to.
Name of the domain event.
Kind of object the event is about, for example a case or document.
Id of the object the event is about.
Id shared with the request and audit records that produced the event.
The event itself as JSON.
Publishing state, written as PENDING, and no code in LexaVault moves it further yet (to confirm).
When the event happened.
When the event row was written.
When the event was published, no code writes it yet (to confirm).
Number of publishing attempts, written as 0 and not changed by any code yet (to confirm).
Error from the last publishing attempt, no code writes it yet (to confirm).

setTableRemarks.remarks: Retention and deletion state of each case: exports done, when the original and redacted files are due for deletion, and holds.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: The case (document package) this lifecycle is for.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
Number of successful exports of the case, capped by the lifecycle policy maximum.
When the case was last exported successfully.
When the original files become due for deletion, set from the last successful export.
When the stored redacted copies become due for deletion, set from the last successful export.
Safety hold for a case never exported: its files are kept until this time, then deleted.
When the redacted copies were deleted.
When the original files were deleted.
When the case's files were finally deleted, after which it can no longer be reprocessed.
Whether a person gave the final delivery approval the entity's policy requires, cleared at each export.
When the lifecycle row was last changed.
Optimistic locking counter, increased on every update.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Fixed record of the document intelligence mode and bundle used for each processing cycle of a case, no document content.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the snapshot.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
The case (document package) that was processed.
Which processing run of the case this is, starting at 1, unique per case.
Intelligence mode the entity's policy asked for: DISABLED, OBSERVE or ENABLED.
Intelligence mode actually used: DISABLED, OBSERVE or ENABLED, DISABLED when it fell back to the baseline.
The intelligence bundle used, the baseline bundle when disabled or on fallback.
Version of the entity's intelligence policy at the time of processing.
Whether intelligence modules were allowed to run (mode not DISABLED).
Whether intelligence could influence decisions (mode ENABLED only).
Whether the baseline detection path had to run, always true in this version.
Whether processing fell back to the baseline because the requested bundle could not run.
When the snapshot was taken.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Which server is processing a case right now, so only one server works on a case at a time.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: The case (document package) being processed.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
Id of the server instance holding the lease.
Number increased on every new lease, so a server with an old lease cannot save results.
When the current lease was taken.
When the holding server last confirmed it is still working.
When the lease runs out if not renewed, after which another server may take the case.
Number of processing attempts for the case, at least 1, checked against the attempt budget.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Why a person rejected a case, as a reason code, one row per case, never free text.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: The rejected case (document package).
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
LV code of the rejection reason: wrong document, unreadable, out of scope, duplicate, or other (see ticket).
The person who rejected the case.
When the case was rejected.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Queue of staged pipeline jobs (TEXT, FIND, VISION, REDACT, EXPORT, SPLIT_EXPORT) per case, with retries and claims, no content.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the job.
The entity (tenant) the job belongs to.
Pipeline stage of the job: TEXT, FIND, VISION, REDACT, EXPORT or SPLIT_EXPORT.
The case (document package) the job works on.
The document the job works on (for SPLIT_EXPORT its source document), empty for a whole-case job.
The integration connection the export is sent to, empty for the local export folder.
For SPLIT_EXPORT the derived delivery id, empty otherwise.
The case run (export cycle) the job belongs to, starting at 1.
Pick-up priority: URGENT, NORMAL, LOW or BULK.
Job state: READY, RUNNING, WAITING_RETRY, PAUSED, WAITING_FOR_YOU, NEEDS_IT, DONE or STOPPED.
Number of times the job has been tried.
When the job is next due to run.
Id of the server currently running the job, empty when not claimed.
When the current claim runs out, after which the job can be taken again.
Fencing token increased on every claim, a result is saved only with the current one.
LV error code of the last failure, empty when none.
Internal code with detail on the last result, for example DELIVERY_IO or CLAIM_EXPIRED.
When the job was queued.
When the job was last changed.
Whether the next run is a person's resend, which gets one attempt and goes to IT on failure.
Whether the export was rebuilt from the stored redacted copies, allowed once per job.
Number of claims that ran out because a server stopped mid-job, the job goes to IT after the maximum.
When the job first failed, empty if it never failed.
When the job last failed, used to count recent failures per destination.
Ever-increasing queue number from a sequence, used for pick-up order instead of the clock.
First page of the page batch the job covers, empty with page_to for the whole document.
Last page of the page batch the job covers, empty with page_from for the whole document.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Short-lived locks that stop two workers processing the same document at once, released or left to expire.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Name of the lock, built from what is locked, such as a document id.
The entity (tenant) the locked item belongs to, empty for a lock not tied to one.
Id of the worker holding the lock.
Token of the current holder, needed to release the lock.
When the lock runs out if not released.
When the lock was first taken.
When the lock was last taken or renewed.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Review work items: one per case sent to a person to check its findings before approval.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the review task.
The entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
The case (document package) to review.
Review state: PENDING, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, APPROVED, REJECTED, ESCALATED or CANCELLED.
The person the review is assigned to, empty while unassigned.
When the review task was created.
When the review task was last changed.
Optimistic locking counter, increased on every update.

setTableRemarks.remarks: How every stored file is protected (plain or encrypted), the record decides and a file without one is not opened, the key itself is never here.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Which file store holds the file, part of the key with storage_key.
Path or key of the file within the store, part of the key with storage_provider.
The entity (tenant) the file belongs to.
How the file is stored: PLAIN (development only, and files from before encryption) or ENCRYPTED.
Name of the encryption format of the file, empty when plain.
Version of the encryption format, empty when plain.
Which key service can open the wrapped key, empty when plain.
The customer whose keys encrypted the file, empty when plain.
The file's data key in wrapped form, which only the key service can open, empty when plain.
Version of the customer key used to wrap the data key, empty when plain.
Size of the encrypted file in bytes, checked before the file is read, empty when plain.
SHA-256 of the encrypted file, checked before it is read so a changed file is refused, empty when plain.
When the record was written.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Sealed vault entries: one per document and artifact kind kept in the vault, with checksum, retention and legal hold.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Unique id of the vault entry.
The entity (tenant) the entry belongs to.
The case (document package) the entry belongs to.
The document the entry belongs to.
The artifact (file) the entry keeps.
Kind of artifact kept, typically REDACTED or ORIGINAL, unique per document.
Algorithm used for checksum_value, for example SHA-256.
Checksum registered for the artifact, used to verify its integrity later.
Minimum number of days the entry must be kept.
Maximum number of days the entry may be kept, empty for no maximum.
Whether the entry is under legal hold and must not be deleted.
Whether the entry is sealed and can no longer be changed.
When the entry was sealed.
When the entry was registered in the vault.
Optimistic locking counter, increased on every update.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Intake sources an entity has marked as Bulk, with the daily window in which their cases may run (cases from them get priority BULK).

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Entity (tenant) that marked the source as Bulk.
The source: an integration connection id, or folder:<key> for a watched folder.
Start of the daily window, in the entity's local time, in which this source's Bulk cases may be processed.
End of the daily window, in the entity's local time (never equal to window_from).
True when Bulk cases of this source may also run all day on weekends, outside the weekday window.
When the source was marked as Bulk or its window last changed.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Links an approval request sent to supervisors to the case and case version it asks to approve for delivery. Ids only.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Id of the approval request held by the platform notifications service.
Entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
The case (document package) awaiting final approval before delivery.
Version of the case the request was raised for, so each version is asked about only once.
When the approval request was created.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Each attempt to deliver a case submission to the main destination, with its outcome.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the attempt.
The delivery submission this attempt belongs to.
Sequence number of the attempt within its submission, starting at 1.
Integration connection used for the attempt, null when no connection applies (local export folder).
Configuration version of the connection at the time of the attempt.
Attempt outcome: STARTED, SUCCEEDED, FAILED_RETRYABLE or FAILED_ATTENTION.
Category code of the failure when the attempt failed, no content.
When the attempt started.
When the attempt finished, null while it runs.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Each redacted document included in a delivery submission, with its checksum and the destination's acknowledgement.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the row.
The delivery submission the document belongs to.
Entity (tenant) the document belongs to.
The case (document package) being delivered.
The LexaVault document being delivered.
Stable id LexaVault sends for this document (doc-<uuid>), used by the destination to recognise repeats.
File name sent with the redacted document.
Size in bytes of the redacted file sent.
Algorithm of the checksum sent, for example SHA-256.
Checksum of the redacted file sent, used by the destination to verify it.
True once the destination has acknowledged receiving this document.
The destination's own id for the received document, when it returned one.
Where the destination says it stored the document, when it returned one.
When the destination acknowledged the document.

setTableRemarks.remarks: One delivery of a case's redacted documents to the main destination per export cycle, with its status and progress.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the submission.
Entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
The case (document package) being delivered.
Export cycle (case run) the submission belongs to, one submission per case and cycle.
Stable id LexaVault sends for the submission (sub-<uuid>), used by the destination to detect repeats.
Kind of destination delivered to, for example document-store.
Submission state: PENDING, DELIVERING, PARTIALLY_ACKNOWLEDGED, RETRY_PENDING, DELIVERED or ATTENTION_REQUIRED.
Number of delivery attempts made so far.
The destination's own id for the submission, when it returned one.
Category code of the latest failure, no content.
When the submission was created.
When the submission last changed.
When the submission was fully delivered.
JSON record of how far the delivery got through the destination profile (calls made, the destination's ids), null for older rows.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Split documents made from pages matched by a routing rule, and their delivery to the rule's destination.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the derived delivery.
Entity (tenant) the case belongs to.
The case (document package) the pages come from.
The LexaVault document whose pages were split out.
Export cycle (case run) the derived delivery belongs to.
Routing rule that matched, set to null if the rule is deleted.
Integration connection the split document is delivered to.
Configuration version of the destination connection when the delivery was planned.
Copy of the rule's destination label at the time of the split.
Copy of the rule's marker type: BARCODE, QR_CODE or TEXT_PATTERN.
Copy of the rule's marker value that was matched.
Page numbers of the source document included in the split document.
Stored artifact holding the redacted split document.
Stable id LexaVault sends for the split document, its idempotency key at the destination.
File name sent with the split document.
Delivery state: PENDING, DELIVERING, RETRY_PENDING, DELIVERED or ATTENTION_REQUIRED.
Number of delivery attempts made so far.
Category code of the latest failure, no content.
True when a failed delivery may be tried again.
The destination's own reference for the delivered document, when it returned one.
When the derived delivery was created.
When the derived delivery last changed.
When the split document was delivered.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Each attempt to deliver a split (derived) document, with its outcome.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the attempt.
The derived delivery this attempt belongs to.
Sequence number of the attempt, starting at 1.
Integration connection used for the attempt.
Configuration version of the connection at the time of the attempt.
Attempt outcome: STARTED, SUCCESS or FAILED.
Category code of the failure when the attempt failed, no content.
When the attempt started.
When the attempt finished, null while it runs.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Each document written by a successful case export, with its checksum and where it was put.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the row.
The case export record (package_export_records) this document belongs to.
Entity (tenant) the document belongs to.
The case (document package) exported.
The LexaVault document exported.
File name of the exported redacted document.
Size in bytes of the exported file.
Algorithm of the checksum, for example SHA-256.
Checksum of the exported file.
Where the file was placed at the destination (path or destination reference).

setTableRemarks.remarks: Current health of each export destination used by the export queue (no row means WORKING). Codes, ids and times only.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Integration connection id of the destination, or an id derived from the tenant id for the local export folder.
Entity (tenant) the destination belongs to.
Destination state: WORKING, PAUSED (transient failures, a probe brings it back) or NEEDS_IT (sign-in refused, waits for IT).
When the destination was last paused.
Number of failures in a row, used to decide when to pause.
When a probe last checked whether a paused destination is back.
LexaVault error code (LV-...) of the latest failure.
When the row last changed.
After a rate-limit answer (429), no job for this destination is taken before this time.
Workers taken off this destination after rate limiting, never leaving fewer than one, restored one by one after quiet periods.
When the destination last answered with a rate limit (429).
When the destination's own check last failed, used by the all-destinations-unreachable rule.

setTableRemarks.remarks: One row per entity for the alert that LexaVault cannot reach any of its export destinations.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Entity (tenant) the alert is for.
RAISED while every destination fails its check, CLEARED when any check passes.
When the alert was last raised.
When the destinations were last checked for this alert.
When the alert was last cleared.
When the row last changed.

setTableRemarks.remarks: How long exported copies are kept per export destination (1 to 72 hours), with one master row per entity.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the row.
Entity (tenant) the setting belongs to.
Split (routing) destination's connection id, or null for the master destination.
Retention period in hours, between 1 and 72.
Actor id of the person who last changed the setting.
When the setting last changed.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Each document announced by an external intake, tracked until its PDF arrives.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the row.
The external intake (and case) the document belongs to.
The sender's own id for the document, unique within the intake.
File name given by the sender.
SHA-256 the sender declared for the file, checked on arrival when given.
The LexaVault document created when the file arrived.
SHA-256 of the file actually received.
Sender's idempotency key for the upload, so a repeated upload is recognised.
When the file arrived.
Sensitivity level the document was announced with: STANDARD, CONFIDENTIAL or HIGHLY_CONFIDENTIAL.

setTableRemarks.remarks: A case announced by an external sender (push API, polling or scanner), tracked until all its documents arrive or it expires.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: The case (document package) created for the intake.
Entity (tenant) the intake belongs to.
Integration connection (source) the intake came through.
How the intake arrived: PUSH_API, POLLING or SCANNER.
The sender's own id for the package.
The sender's revision of the package, so a changed package is taken as a new intake.
Attempt number for the same package and revision, starting at 1.
SHA-256 hex fingerprint of the intake request, used to recognise repeats of the same request.
Intake state: AWAITING_DOCUMENTS, ACCEPTED_FOR_PROCESSING or INCOMPLETE_EXPIRED.
When the intake was announced.
When an incomplete intake expires (from the connection's incomplete window).
When all documents arrived and the case was accepted for processing.
When the intake expired incomplete.
When the files of an expired intake were cleaned up.
When the row last changed.

setTableRemarks.remarks: What the watched folder intake saw for each drop: waiting, accepted, refused or duplicate, and why.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the row.
Entity (tenant) the drop belongs to.
Reference to the drop in the watched folder (its folder or file name).
Observation state: WAITING_FOR_TRIGGER, ACCEPTED, REJECTED or DUPLICATE.
Why a drop was refused, an IntakeRejectionCode name such as MISSING_FILE or INVALID_FILE.
Fingerprint of the drop, so a resumed drop continues its existing case instead of counting as a duplicate.
The case (document package) created from the drop, when one was.
When the drop was first seen.
Time before which a drop still waiting for its trigger file is left out of the intake list.
When the row last changed.

setTableRemarks.remarks: What intake refused or had already taken in, per source system: the LV code and time only. Watched folder drops are in intake_observations.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the row.
Entity (tenant) the refusal belongs to.
The source: an integration connection id, or type:MANUAL_UPLOAD for manual uploads.
LexaVault error code (LV-...) of the refusal.
REFUSED or DUPLICATE (already taken in).
When the refusal happened.

setTableRemarks.remarks: Each entity's configured connections to senders (intake sources) and destinations (delivery), without any secret value.

setColumnRemarks.remarks: Primary key of the connection.
Entity (tenant) the connection belongs to.
Name of the connection, unique within the entity.
Optional description of the connection.
What the connection is for: INGESTION_SOURCE, DOCUMENT_STORE_DELIVERY or DERIVED_DOCUMENT_DELIVERY.
INBOUND (sender) or OUTBOUND (destination).
Transport family: PUSH_API, HTTP_API, FILE_SHARE, WATCHED_FOLDER or SCANNER.
How the connection authenticates: NONE, BASIC, API_KEY, JWT, OAUTH2_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS or MTLS.
Machine client identity the sender signs in with, unique within the entity.
Address of the remote system for HTTP connections.
Root folder path for file share connections.
Reference to where the connection's secret is stored outside the database, never the secret itself.
Timeout in seconds for calls to the remote system.
Maximum number of retries for a failed call.
Hours an external intake may wait for its documents before it expires.
Most documents one intake from this source may hold, capped at the case limit.
Largest PDF in bytes accepted from this source.
Most pages per PDF accepted from this source, capped at the case limit.
What counts as acknowledgement: NONE, HTTP_SUCCESS, DESTINATION_RECEIPT, DURABLE_FILE_WRITE, SOURCE_PICKUP_ACK or SUBMISSION_ACK.
True when the connection is in use.
Version number raised on each configuration change, recorded with each delivery attempt.
Last known health: UNKNOWN, HEALTHY, DEGRADED, UNAVAILABLE or DISABLED.
When the connection last worked.
When the connection last failed.
